title: Eosinophil-to-neutrophil log balance does not establish incremental continuous CRP prediction across two NHANES samples
abstract: A source-frozen model trained on 4,089 NHANES 2005–2006 adults was tested in 5,181 separately sampled 2007–2008 adults. Adding log((eosinophils+0.05)/(neutrophils+0.05)) to demographic, adiposity, smoking and standard leukocyte-index predictors changed survey-weighted log-CRP RMSE from 1.058080 to 1.057865. Improvement 0.000216, joint source-refit/target PSU-bootstrap95% interval [-0.001461, 0.001833], did not establish incremental benefit. The balance is algebraically determined by its component counts; no novel physiological information or clinical utility is established.
